title: How a Microphone Works in 60 Seconds 🎤🧲 #shorts
description:
A microphone turns your voice into electricity. Sound waves shake a thin diaphragm, the diaphragm moves a tiny coil of wire around a magnet, and that motion induces an electric current shaped exactly like the sound, ready to be amplified or recorded. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#microphone #howitworks #shorts

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: A microphone is basically a *speaker* running in *reverse*.

steps.label: Sound
steps.text: When you talk, your voice pushes *pressure waves* through the air toward the mic.

steps.label: Diaphragm
steps.text: They hit a thin *diaphragm*, making it shake back and forth with your *voice*.

steps.label: Coil
steps.text: A tiny *coil* of wire is glued to it, sliding around a strong *magnet*.

steps.label: Induction
steps.text: Wire moving through a magnetic field makes *electricity*. That's called *induction*.

steps.label: Signal
steps.text: The current copies the shape of the *sound wave*, so it can be *amplified* and recorded.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Air, coil, *current*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
